## Answer: $(N+1)(2N+1)^2$

**Construction.** Colour a unit cube at position $(x,y,z)$ black exactly when $z$ is odd. Every $2\times2\times2$ block spans two consecutive $z$-layers, one odd and one even. The odd layer contributes 4 black cubes and the even layer contributes 0, so each such block has exactly 4 black cubes. The cube has $N+1$ odd layers among $2N+1$ layers, each with $(2N+1)^2$ cubes, giving $(N+1)(2N+1)^2$ black cubes.

**Optimality (not fully verified here).** I did not complete a rigorous upper-bound proof. I checked the case $N=1$ partially: this construction gives 18 black cubes in a $3\times3\times3$ cube, which beats the parity colouring (14). I also recall this as a known competition result with this answer, but I have not verified that no configuration with more black cubes exists for general $N$.

ANSWER: $(N+1)(2N+1)^2$
